name: Paladin
description:
As a paladin, you radiate an aura of unyielding righteousness that strikes fear in the hearts of the wicked.
When confronted with multiple foes, let loose with Total Eclipse or, after attaining level 50, Circle of Scorn to inflict Enmity en masse. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Paladin Combo and Rage of Halone. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Total Eclipse, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low.
Should you need to inflict Enmity on a foe in a pinch, Spirits Within or Provoke will do the trick. You don't always need to have Enmity on every enemy in an encounter, however. There's little point in spending an action to inflict Enmity on a foe if you expect them to fall during one of your allies' turns.
Once per round, you can use Sturdy Shield when an enemy attacks you with an ability to add 1 d6 to your Defense. With a little luck, you may even be able to negate a direct hit from a physical ability, so be sure to make use of this instant ability whenever you can.

name: Warrior
description:
Like a raging maelstrom sweeping the field of battle, warriors command the full attention of their opponents.
When confronted with multiple foes, charge into the fray and use Overpower to inflict Enmity on the lot of them. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage or an instant ability to replenish your HP.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Warrior Combo and Storm's Path. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Overpower, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low. Storm's Path dishes out damage while restoring HP—a surefire way to stay hale and hearty in the heat of battle while also helping hack down your foes.
With an arsenal that includes the Surging Tempest enhancement and the Berserk secondary ability, warriors are well equipped to dish out more damage than other tanks. You'll also have a lot of opportunities to accumulate Wrath as the encounter plays out, which can be spent to unleash powerful abilities that can really bring the pain. As the oft-repeated saying goes, the best defense is a good offense, so raise your axe high and lay your foes low.

name: Dark Knight
description:
Driven to seek justice at any cost, dark knights call upon the darkness within to vanquish those who would stand in their way.
When confronted with multiple foes, wade into the thick of battle and use Unleash to inflict Enmity on all around you. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart or, after attaining level 40, Shadow Wall as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Dark Knight Combo and Souleater. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Unleash, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low. Souleater deals damage while restoring HP, allowing you to stay on your feet while cutting down your foes.
The Darkside enhancement lets you spend MP for a chance to boost your damage output. This can quickly drain your reserves, so make sure to use abilities that replenish MP whenever you need a top-up in order to get the most out of this unique enhancement.
Unlike other tanks, dark knights are capable of bringing both physical and magic abilities to bear against their foes. As the enemies you encounter are often more resilient against one of these at the expense of the other, learning to quickly recognize which type of ability is more effective in a given situation will undoubtedly prove a boon.

name: White Mage
description:
Wielders of the purifying art of white magic, white mages ensure their allies never falter in the face of adversity.
Though you may be tempted to use Cure II to restore a significant amount of HP to a wounded tank or other ally, keep in mind that any healing that exceeds the target's Max HP will go to waste. As a healer, your MP is a vital resource that can make the difference between victory and defeat in an encounter. If an ally hasn't suffered so much damage that they're in danger of being Knocked Out, consider conserving your MP by healing them with a simple Cure instead. After attaining level 40, the ability check for Cure has a chance to proc Freecure, which in turn reduces the cost of your next Cure II to 0 MP.
You can also inflict DOTs by using Aero, which becomes Aero II after attaining level 50. Granting allies Revivify with Regen—or Medica II after attaining level 50—can be a great way to be proactive with your healing, too. These effects last until the end of the phase, which means the earlier you get them up, the greater impact they'll have in the grand scheme of the encounter.
Learn to divide your attention between healing your allies and harrying your foes, and you'll ensure your party always emerges triumphant.

name: Scholar
description:
As a scholar, your tactical prowess enables you to guide your allies to victory on the field of battle, all the while mending their wounds in tandem with your summoned faerie.
Your pet, the faerie Eos, takes her turn immediately before you, so you'll constantly need to consider where to position her and which of her abilities to have her use. So long as you haven't used Dissipation—which you gain access to after attaining level 60—Eos will aid you in healing your allies for the entirety of an encounter.
Of course, your own abilities do more than simply restore HP—scholars specialize in erecting barriers that prevent their allies from taking damage in the first place, as well as using secondary and instant abilities to chip away at their enemies' HP. Keep in mind that a character cannot have more than one barrier at a time, and when a new barrier is granted, the one with the lower HP value is lost. A wise tactician always keeps a cool head so that they may judge when their barriers are needed and plan accordingly.
After attaining level 50, you gain access to Sacred Soil, an ability that creates an area in which allies suffer reduced damage. This area cannot be moved once deployed, so make use of your tactical ingenuity and select the most favorable position on the encounter map.

name: Astrologian
description:
As an astrologian, you possess the wisdom to influence the fate of your fellow adventurers by interpreting the patterns of the stars in the heavens.
While you are well equipped to keep your allies fighting fit by restoring HP and granting Revivify, you can also support your party by empowering a single ally with Major Arcana at the start of your turn with your Play Arcana trait. Major Arcana allows this ally to reroll a single die when determining the damage dealt by an ability, which improves their chances of inflicting a significant blow to your opposition. Don't forget to make use of your Play Arcana trait at the start of each of your turns to harness your full potential.
You also have several instant abilities that affect all allies within an area around you. Try to position yourself within range of your party members while staying out of your enemies' reach so you can heal up your comrades at a moment's notice and divine the path to victory.

name: Monk
description:
Masters of the fist and the inner power known as chakra, monks draw upon their battle-honed senses and years of intense training to perform devastating martial techniques that demolish their foes.
Monk Combo allows you to attack with blinding speed and use a staggering three abilities in a single turn. Typically, you'll start by using an ability without a condition, followed by one that requires you to be in Raptor Form, then finish with one that requires Coeurl Form. Doing so will leave you in Opo-Opo Form at the start of your next turn. If you use Bootshine while in Opo-Opo Form and it results in a direct hit, you automatically score a critical as well, drastically increasing its destructive power. After attaining level 40, each critical also grants you Chakra.
Certain abilities will grant you stacks of Opo-Opo's Fury, Raptor's Fury, and Coeurl's Fury, which can then be spent to deal additional damage and reposition when using abilities that enable your Bestial Fury trait.
After attaining level 60, you gain access to the powerful Masterful Blitz ability. Before you can unleash it, however, you'll need to use Perfect Balance to gain Beast Chakra. On the following turn, you can then use Masterful Blitz to unleash a destructive monk technique.
Master your forms, make skillful use of your Bestial Fury trait, and open your Beast Chakra to let loose with Masterful Blitz to leap like an opo-opo, rise like a raptor, and pounce like a coeurl in the heat of battle.

name: Dragoon
description:
Trained to do battle with mighty dragons high above the clouds, dragoons leap swiftly across the battlefield, their spears ever poised to strike.
When enemies draw near, hit them with True Thrust, then use your Combo trait to attack once more. Using Disembowel grants you Power Surge, which increases the damage dealt by all of your abilities, so be sure to use it before mounting a major offensive.
When your enemies have retreated beyond your reach, you can use Jump or, after attaining level 50, Dragonfire Dive to strike from afar. These abilities can deal significant damage, so consider using Life Surge beforehand to give yourself an advantage die on your ability check and better your chances of scoring a direct hit or a critical.
With both Elusive Jump, attained at level 40, and, after attaining level 50, Winged Glide at your disposal, you can traverse the encounter map with nigh-unrestricted freedom. Just remember that Elusive Jump comes with the risk of ending up in a less than advantageous position.

name: Ninja
description:
Ninjas are nimble fighters who employ deadly twin daggers alongside mystical shinobi techniques known as ninjutsu to strike at their foes from the shadows.
After using Ritual Weave to gain Mudra, you can spend that Mudra to use Ninjutsu and execute one of your many ninjutsu. A well-timed application of these skills can turn the tides of battle, so learn your capabilities inside and out and stay alert for the perfect opportunity to strike. After attaining level 50, combining the trait Swift of Hand with a focus action will allow you to use Ritual Weave three times in a single turn, giving you access to an even wider array of ninjutsu.
Keep in mind that all ninjutsu techniques require preparation, and as such, Ninjutsu cannot be used twice in quick succession. On turns when Ninjutsu is unavailable, make use of your Ninja Combo and utilize the Combo trait to slice through the opposition.
Your finely honed senses allow you to anticipate when an encounter is about to break out, so you typically start your first turn Hidden. This allows you to strike down foes unseen with Trick Attack, which also grants you an advantage die on your next ability check and provides the perfect opportunity to unleash a powerful ninjutsu.
You also boast a practical kit of instant abilities, which, when used wisely, will allow you to undermine your foes. You can use Shukuchi when your enemies are out of reach to close the distance in a flash, and Shade Shift to give you a chance to shrug off a direct hit, improving your overall survivability. When an enemy is on their last legs, don't forget to put them out of their misery with a lethal Assassinate.

name: Bard
description:
As a bard, your songs resound across the battlefield, inspiring your allies and bolstering their courage.
Like other physical ranged DPS jobs, you have a multitude of abilities that can damage or otherwise hamper your foes. On your turn, you can make use of your Arrow Flurry trait to attack not once, but twice with your flurry abilities. Venomous Bite + Windbite inflicts a potent DOT, while Straight Shot and Wide Volley pack a significant punch, though they can only be used while under the effect of Hawk's Eye. And when your enemies are on their last legs, you can use Barrage to let loose a volley of powerful attacks and win the day for you and yours.
But what sets you apart from other projectile slingers is your capacity for empowering your allies through song. At the start of your turn, the Bardsong trait allows you to break into song, granting a song effect that benefits the entire party. Take care to remind your allies of the effects a given song confers, lest they forget to take them into account!

name: Machinist
description:
As a machinist, you excel at picking off foes from afar with an arsenal of firearms and technological weaponry inspired by Garlond Ironworks' magitek.
Thanks to the Mechanized Sharpshooter trait, there is no limit to the number of instant abilities you may use on your turn. This allows you to concentrate your considerable toolkit into a single, heavily damaging fusillade of physical firepower that few foes can withstand.
After attaining level 40, you can use Smoking Barrel to fire off three Heat Blast attacks in a single turn. Combine this with Gauss Round each time you do so, and you'll riddle your foes with a seemingly endless barrage of bullets.
Reassemble allows you to guarantee a critical for a single ability, so long as the action isn't interrupted. Remember to Reassemble your weapon before using an ability with base and direct hit effects that allow you to roll a great many dice when dealing damage.
After attaining level 40, certain abilities start granting you Battery Charges, which you can use to deploy a machine that will automatically attack your foes. Between your own firepower and the support provided by your machine, your enemies will find you a formidable foe indeed.

name: Black Mage
description:
As a black mage, you wield the destructive powers of black magic with ease, annihilating those who would oppose you with its elemental fury.
Like all magical ranged DPS, you excel at striking down distant foes—be they alone or in groups—using powerful magic abilities. Black mages can forgo all standard movement on their turn in order to use an additional invoked primary ability, so you'll generally want to take up a safe position from which to cast, moving only when absolutely necessary.
Most of your fire-aspected and ice-aspected abilities will grant you the effects of traits that affect your damage output and MP recovery. Astral Fire increases the damage dealt by your fire-aspected abilities but prevents you from recovering MP naturally, while Umbral Ice restores MP when you attack with ice-aspected abilities. You can switch between Astral Fire and Umbral Ice as needed by using Transpose.
You are not, of course, limited to the elements of fire and ice alone. Changing between Astral Fire and Umbral Ice grants you the Thunderhead Ready enhancement, which allows you to use a thunder spell ability as a secondary action. With mastery over the elements, you will have little trouble subjugating your foes with raging fire, freezing blizzards, and crackling lightning.

name: Summoner
description:
As a summoner, you draw upon the essence of primals to call forth arcane familiars ready to do your bidding.
During encounters, your pet takes its turn immediately before you, so you'll constantly need to consider where to position it and which of its abilities to have it use. Though you will typically fight alongside your pet Carbuncle, you have the ability to call upon other familiars as well. Using Aethercharge grants you Gemstone Arcanum, which allows you to imbue your Carbuncle with aspected aether—fire for Ifrit, earth for Titan, and wind for Garuda at the start of its turn. Doing so will transform it into an aspected Carbuncle of a different hue, or, after attaining level 40, an egi, a manifestation of a primal's essence.
While transformed, your pet has access to more powerful abilities, and its newly aspected form enhances your gem abilities. As such, you'll want to alternate between turns in which you use Aethercharge and those in which you use your powered-up gem abilities.
After attaining level 60, you can infuse your essence with that of the dreadwyrm Bahamut by using Dreadwyrm Trance. Keep in mind that you cannot use Dreadwyrm Trance while an egi is summoned.
